hints.title: Extracting an Element Difference
hints.text: Sort the subset sums. The difference between sums[1] and sums[0] is the absolute value of some element d in the original array.

hints.title: Partitioning Into Paired Sets
hints.text: Partition all sums into two multisets S0 and S1 such that each element in S1 equals an element in S0 plus d.

hints.title: Recursing on the Subproblem Containing Zero
hints.text: The subset sum of the empty set is 0. If 0 is in S0, d is positive and we recurse on S0. If 0 is in S1, -d is in the original array.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from collections import Counter

class Solution:
    def recoverArray(self, n: int, sums: list[int]) -> list[int]:
        sums.sort()
        ans = []
        for _ in range(n):
            d = sums[1] - sums[0]
            count = Counter(sums)
            s0, s1 = [], []
            for x in sums:
                if count[x] > 0:
                    s0.append(x)
                    s1.append(x + d)
                    count[x] -= 1
                    count[x + d] -= 1
            if 0 in s0:
                ans.append(d)
                sums = s0
            else:
                ans.append(-d)
                sums = s1
        return ans
```

variables: N: number of elements in the target array
complexity.notes: Partitioning 2^N elements across N divide-and-conquer steps.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing 2^N subset combinations with exhaustive search is intractable for N up to 15.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Greedy multiset pairing with Counter identifies individual elements one by one.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that adjacent sorted subset sums expose an element difference and use divide-and-conquer.
